Random interval of SPI, ER or IR at a scar count

Source: R/random_interval.R
random_interval.Rd

Returns the central 95% interval of an index for a core whose scar directions are uniform on the sphere, at each requested scar count. A raw reading outside this interval departs from what random directions produce at that scar count; a reading inside it cannot be told apart from random directions at that scar count.

Usage

random_interval(parameter = c("SPI", "ER", "IR"), n)

Arguments

parameter

Character vector: "SPI", "ER" and/or "IR" (case-insensitive).

n

Scar counts (whole numbers). Counts below 3 give NA.

Value

A tibble with one row per combination of parameter and n: parameter, n, lower (2.5th percentile) and upper (97.5th percentile).

Details

The interval narrows as the scar count grows, so a raw value can only be judged against the interval of its own scar count. compute_spi(), compute_ei() and spi_ei_batch() look the interval up for you.

SPI is computed from its exact distribution (the resultant length of n unit vectors uniform on the sphere), ER and IR from 5000 simulated random cores per scar count. Values for n = 3 to 200 are tabulated; SPI above 200 is computed on the fly; ER and IR above 200 are NA.

Which side of the interval indicates organisation depends on the index: SPI and ER above the upper bound, and IR below the lower bound, indicate scar directions more concentrated than random. SPI below the lower bound is typical of opposed (bidirectional) flaking.

References

Rayleigh, Lord (1919). On the problem of random vibrations, and of random flights in one, two, or three dimensions. Philosophical Magazine, 37(220), 321–347.

See also

compute_spi(), compute_ei(), spi_ei_batch(), plot_random_interval()

Examples

random_interval("SPI", n = c(6, 20))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   parameter     n  lower upper
#>   <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 SPI           6 0.114  0.692
#> 2 SPI          20 0.0607 0.390
random_interval(c("ER", "IR"), n = 10)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   parameter     n  lower upper
#>   <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 ER           10 0.0800 0.653
#> 2 IR           10 0.120  0.632
